local_market_longform:
Austin is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in Austin currently trade around a median of $530,000 and take roughly 48 days to go under contract, with about 22% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. Austin runs heavily to 1920s–1940s bungalows in central east and Hyde Park, post-war ranches, and rapid 2000s–2020s construction, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around Austin, the issues we see most are expansive-clay foundation movement, flash-flood risk in low-lying creeks, extreme-heat wear, and rocky-soil grading issues. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like East Austin out to Round Rock and Pflugerville — and in Texas the local economy anchored by tech (Tesla, Oracle, Apple, Samsung), the University of Texas, and state government keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Travis County, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the Austin sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near the Texas State Capitol also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen Austin. We know what a block in East Austin, Montopolis, Dove Springs, and Hyde Park actually sells for, what Central Texas buyers will and won't pay for, and how Travis County's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

situations.title: Relocating
situations.body: A job change shouldn't mean carrying two mortgages or managing a sale from a thousand miles away. Close on your schedule and move on.

situations.title: Inherited a house in Austin
situations.body: Settling an estate — often from out of state — is hard enough without a listing on top of it. We buy inherited Austin homes as-is, work alongside the Travis County probate process, and let you take what matters and leave the rest.

situations.title: Facing foreclosure
situations.body: If you're behind on payments in Travis County, a fast cash sale can settle the loan before it hits your credit. We move on your timeline, not the bank's.

situations.title: Downsizing or aging in place
situations.body: When a longtime East Austin-area home has become too much to keep up, we make a fair offer and let you set a move-out date that isn't rushed.

situations.title: The house needs too much work
situations.body: Fire, water, foundation, or years of deferred repairs — we've bought all of it around Austin. No cleaning, no contractors, no staging.

situations.title: Divorce or a major life change
situations.body: When the goal is simply to have the Austin house handled cleanly and split fairly, we make the sale the simple part.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my Austin house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed Texas title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in Austin pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy Austin homes in any condition — including the expansive-clay foundation movement we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your Austin neighborhood — places like East Austin — the home's condition, and current Central Texas demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in Texas?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. Texas (TREC/SB 2212) requires accurate disclosure of a buyer's equitable interest; our contracts and marketing state clearly that we are a direct buyer.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Travis County sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
